title: Conversion
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: Conversion is the saving turning of a person from sin to God through repentance and faith in Jesus Christ. It marks a real change of direction as the sinner comes out of darkness into life with God.
summary: Conversion is the saving turning of a person from sin to God through repentance and faith in Jesus Christ. It marks a real change of direction as the sinner comes out of darkness into life with God.
christFocus: Jesus Christ is the One to whom sinners turn in conversion. Through Him, God transfers people from darkness to light, from guilt to forgiveness, and from rebellion to life under His lordship.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Conversion describes the sinner’s turning to God in response to the Gospel. It includes repentance from sin and faith in Christ. The direction of life changes because God’s grace has broken into the heart.

Conversion is not merely adopting religious language, joining a church, or improving behavior. It is turning from idols to serve the living and true God. It brings a person under the saving lordship of Christ.

This turning is real but not always identical in outward appearance. Some conversions seem dramatic; others unfold quietly. What matters is that the person comes to Christ and no longer remains willingly turned away from God.

Conversion begins a life of discipleship. Those who turn to Christ continue learning to turn from sin, walk in truth, and live as new creations before God.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Some people mistake religious exposure for conversion. They may know Christian words, attend services, or admire Jesus without truly turning to Him.

This doctrine also gives hope that no one is locked forever in the old direction. God can turn sinners from darkness, addiction, unbelief, idolatry, shame, and rebellion to life in Christ.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Examine whether your life is turned toward Christ. Do not settle for religious familiarity without repentance and faith. Keep turning from idols, sin, and self-rule, and help others see that salvation brings a real change of allegiance to the living God.
